title: Unit quiz: deduction, transformations and Pythagoras
subject: Mathematics
unit: Spring 2: Deduction; rotation and translation; Pythagoras
source: Seeded from mathematics/y9 lesson 51 (Unit quiz: deduction, transformations and Pythagoras (portal quiz, secure mode, written for this unit))
intro: Covers lessons 32 to 51 of Deduction; rotation and translation; Pythagoras. Answer every question. For multiple choice, fill in one circle.

questions.q: Angles of 125°, x and 90° meet at a point. Find x.
questions.a: A) 145°. 360 - 125 - 90 = 145, angles at a point. 55° uses 180° by mistake.

questions.q: Two angles are in matching positions at each crossing. They are
questions.a: A) corresponding: equal. Matching positions (F shape) are corresponding angles, which are equal.

questions.q: An isosceles triangle has a base angle of 52°. The top angle is
questions.a: A) 76°. Two base angles of 52°: 180 - 104 = 76.

questions.q: Sum of the interior angles of a decagon (10 sides)?
Which reason is acceptable in an exam?
questions.a: A) co-interior angles add up to 180°. Only the full fact earns the mark; shapes, looks and the diagram are not reasons.

questions.q: Which shows a statement is true for EVERY triangle?
options: A chain of reasoned steps using general facts
questions.a: A) A chain of reasoned steps using general facts. Only a general argument covers every case; measurement has errors and cannot cover infinitely many triangles.

questions.q: Co-interior angles are 3x and x + 40. Which equation?
questions.a: A) 3x + x + 40 = 180. Co-interior angles add to 180°. 3x = x + 40 would be for equal angles.

questions.q: Which vector moves 2 left and 5 down?
questions.a: A) (-2 / -5). Left is negative across, down is negative up: (-2 / -5). (-5 / -2) swaps the parts.

questions.q: Which is a full description?
questions.a: A) Rotation 90° anticlockwise about (1, 2). It needs the centre, the angle and the direction.

questions.q: A shape is reflected so (1, 4) maps to (1, -2). The mirror line is
questions.a: A) y = 1. The midpoint of y = 4 and y = -2 is y = 1, a horizontal line.

questions.q: Which point is invariant when reflecting in y = 2?
questions.a: A) (5, 2). Points on the line y = 2 do not move; (5, 2) has y = 2.

questions.q: A shape is turned upside down and its handedness is the same. It is a
questions.a: A) rotation. Handedness kept and turned: rotation. A reflection changes handedness.

questions.q: A right-angled triangle has sides 7, 24, 25. The hypotenuse is
questions.a: A) 25. The longest side, opposite the right angle: 25. Check: 49 + 576 = 625 = 25².

questions.q: The hypotenuse with shorter sides 5 cm and 9 cm is about
questions.a: A) 10.3 cm. √(25 + 81) = √106 = 10.3. 106 forgets the square root; 14 adds the sides.

questions.q: Hypotenuse 10, one side 6. The other side is
questions.a: A) 8. √(100 - 36) = √64 = 8. 11.7 adds; 64 forgets the root.

questions.q: Which is a Pythagorean triple?
A 13 m rope from the top of a pole is pegged 5 m from its base. The pole's height?
questions.a: A) 12 m. The rope is the hypotenuse: √(169 - 25) = 12.

questions.q: Distance from (0, 0) to (3, 4)?
questions.a: A) 5. √(9 + 16) = 5. 7 adds the differences.

questions.q: The angles of an isosceles triangle are x, x and 40°. x =
questions.a: A) 70°. 2x + 40 = 180, x = 70. 40 assumes the wrong angle is repeated.
